title: Interacting Spiral Galaxies NGC 2207 and IC 2163
caption: The interacting spiral galaxies NGC 2207 and IC 2163, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Location not published by the source
credit: NASA, ESA, and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: Two spiral galaxies sit side by side in the direction of the constellation Canis Major, caught as they swing close past each other. The larger and more massive of the pair, on the left, is NGC 2207. IC 2163, the smaller galaxy, sits to its right.

The encounter has not been gentle on the smaller galaxy. Powerful tidal forces from NGC 2207 have pulled IC 2163 out of shape, throwing stars and gas into long streamers that run toward the right-hand edge of the frame and stretch a hundred thousand light-years. A tidal force arises because gravity pulls harder on the near side of a galaxy than on the far side, so the galaxy is stretched along the line between the two.

Hubble recorded the near-collision with its Wide Field Planetary Camera 2, and the Hubble Heritage Team assembled the picture. A spiral galaxy is a flat disc of stars and gas with arms winding out from its centre.
scale: The streamers pulled out of IC 2163 stretch about a hundred thousand light-years, according to NASA.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field Planetary Camera 2 recorded the pair. The colour mapping is not published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers far more light than the eye can collect.
